implementation_notes: The .proto artifact is the published language and protoc --java_out generates immutable message classes: Order.parseFrom(bytes) checks the wire form by construction, writeTo() publishes it, getDescriptor() exposes the schema at runtime, and unknown fields are preserved across binary round-trips. Choose it when several runtimes share one contract and evolution is additive; the JSON/contract-first variant is better when the language is an OpenAPI/JSON Schema document consumed by web clients. The hand-written DTO plus ObjectMapper form is still justified for thin adapters over legacy XML or JSON services.
pitfalls: Generated Java message classes are immutable and verbose: constructing them builder-style inside domain logic couples the domain to the wire schema - translate at the seam instead.
Field numbers are the contract: reserve retired numbers (reserved 4, 7;) or a later participant silently misreads the old tag as a new field.
The protobuf-java runtime version is a deployment-wide constraint (generated code and runtime must match), and shaded/repackaged protobuf jars break descriptor lookups at runtime.

variants.name: Contract-first JSON with Jackson binding and JSON Schema validation
variants.idiom_name: ObjectMapper POJO binding + JsonSchemaFactory/JsonSchema.validate against the published schema
variants.implementation_notes: Contract-first JSON: the language is a JSON Schema/OpenAPI document, Jackson binds payloads to POJOs (@JsonProperty for wire names, unknown-property behaviour configured explicitly) and the payload is validated against the published schema before it reaches the domain (JsonSchemaFactory.getInstance(VersionFlag.V202012).getSchema(node).validate(instance) returns a Set<ValidationMessage>). Unlike codegen the schema stays external, so the contract can be republished without a build - at the cost of reflection-based, runtime-only checking. Prefer it for web-facing APIs whose schema is shared with non-Java clients.
pitfalls: Enabling Jackson default typing for polymorphic published payloads turns a schema field into a gadget-chain entry point; keep any type resolution on an explicit allow-list.

FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES defaults to true, which rejects producer additions - the opposite of the tolerance a published language usually promises; set it deliberately and document the choice in the compatibility policy.
Jackson maps JSON numbers to the POJO field type: overflowing ids or money through double silently loses precision, so use BigInteger/BigDecimal or string-encoded values at the seam.
